```plato
    //==
    // # Choosing a pattern by name
    //
    // One entry point behind the `SamplePattern` enumeration, for the caller who
    // wants to compare strategies rather than configure one. Each case is given
    // the conventional parameters of its family, so the only knobs are the region,
    // a count and a seed; a caller who wants a base, a jitter or a radius builds
    // the pattern record instead.

    // The grid closest to `count` cells over the region, with cells as square as
    // the region's shape allows. Its cell count is at least `count` and may
    // exceed it, because the rows have to divide the columns evenly.
    PatternGrid(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer): IntegerVector2
    {
        var width = (region.Max.X - region.Min.X).Max(0.0);
        var height = (region.Max.Y - region.Min.Y).Max(0.0);
        var columns = count <= 0 || width <= 0.0 || height <= 0.0
            ? 1
            : (count.ToNumber * width / height).Sqrt.Ceiling.ToInteger.Max(1);
        return IntegerVector2(columns, (count.Max(0) + columns - 1) / columns);
    }

    // About `count` points of the named strategy over the region. The families
    // whose count is an input honour it exactly; the grid families report the
    // cells of the nearest grid, and Poisson-disk reports whatever its radius
    // saturated at. The strategies that carry no randomness ignore the seed.
    PatternPoints2D(pattern: SamplePattern, region: Bounds2D, count: Integer,
        seed: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => match (pattern) {
            RegularGrid => JitteredGridPoints2D(region, PatternGrid(region, count), 0.0, seed);
            JitteredGrid => JitteredGridPoints2D(region, PatternGrid(region, count), 1.0, seed);
            Stratified => StratifiedPoints2D(region, PatternGrid(region, count), 1, seed);
            PoissonDisk => PoissonDiskPoints2D(region, BlueNoiseRadius(region, count), 30, seed);
            Halton => HaltonPoints2D(region, count, 2, 3);
            Hammersley => HammersleyPoints2D(region, count, 2);
            Sobol => SobolPoints2D(region, count, 1);
            Plastic => PlasticPoints2D(region, count, 0.5);
            BlueNoise => BlueNoisePoints2D(region, count, seed);
        };

    //==
    // # Quality readings
    //
    // Measurements that let a caller ARGUE that a pattern is blue rather than
    // assert it. Three independent readings, because each one is fooled by
    // something the others catch: spacing says nothing about anisotropy,
    // discrepancy rewards the lattice-like patterns that look worst, and the
    // spectrum is the only one that separates "even" from "regular".

    // The distance from point `index` to the nearest other point, or the largest
    // representable number when there is no other point. The per-point reading a
    // caller histograms: uniform random points give an exponential-looking
    // histogram with mass at zero, and a blue-noise set gives a narrow bump with
    // nothing below its radius.
    NearestNeighborDistance(index: Integer, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
        => points.Count.Range.Reduce(Number.MaxValue, (best, j) =>
            j == index ? best : best.Min(points[index].Distance(points[j])));

    // The spacing a perfect hexagonal packing of `count` points would have over
    // the region: the yardstick the two readings below divide by, so that they
    // compare across counts and across regions.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_packing
    ReferenceSpacing(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer): Number
        => count <= 0 ? 0.0 : (2.0 * RegionArea(region) / (count.ToNumber * Number.SqrtThree)).Sqrt;

    // The relative radius: the smallest distance between any two points, as a
    // fraction of `ReferenceSpacing`. The single number that says how blue a
    // pattern is. A hexagonal lattice reads 1 by definition and a square grid
    // reads about 0.93. A maximal Poisson-disk set lands somewhat below that,
    // near its own radius over the reference spacing. Uniform random points and a
    // fully jittered grid both read near zero, for the same reason: two
    // independent draws can land arbitrarily close, and one pair doing so is
    // enough. Fewer than two points read zero.
    RelativeRadius(region: Bounds2D, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
    {
        var reference = ReferenceSpacing(region, points.Count);
        var smallest = points.Count.Range.Reduce(Number.MaxValue, (best, i) =>
            best.Min(NearestNeighborDistance(i, points)));
        return points.Count < 2 || reference <= 0.0 ? 0.0 : smallest / reference;
    }

    // The mean nearest-neighbour distance as a fraction of `ReferenceSpacing`.
    // A Poisson process expects a mean nearest-neighbour distance of half the
    // reciprocal square root of the density, which puts this reading a little
    // under one half; it climbs toward 1 as a pattern approaches the hexagonal
    // packing. Reported beside the relative radius because the two disagree in
    // the interesting case: one close pair drags the radius to zero and leaves
    // the mean untouched, so a pattern that is evenly spaced APART FROM one
    // accident reads high here and low there.
    RelativeMeanSpacing(region: Bounds2D, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
    {
        var reference = ReferenceSpacing(region, points.Count);
        var total = SumOf(points.Count.MapRange(i => NearestNeighborDistance(i, points)));
        return points.Count < 2 || reference <= 0.0 ? 0.0
            : total / points.Count.ToNumber / reference;
    }

    // The local discrepancy of the box anchored at the region's minimum corner and
    // reaching to `corner`: how far the fraction of points inside it is from the
    // fraction of the area it covers.
    BoxDiscrepancy(corner: Point2D, region: Bounds2D, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
    {
        var area = RegionArea(region);
        var box = (corner.X - region.Min.X).Max(0.0) * (corner.Y - region.Min.Y).Max(0.0);
        var inside = points.Reduce(0.0, (n, p) =>
            n + (p.X <= corner.X && p.Y <= corner.Y ? 1.0 : 0.0));
        return points.Count <= 0 || area <= 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : (inside / points.Count.ToNumber - box / area).Abs;
    }

    // An estimate of the star discrepancy: the largest local discrepancy over the
    // boxes whose far corner is one of the sample points. Lower is better, and
    // the low-discrepancy families are the ones that win it — which is exactly why
    // it is reported next to the spacing readings rather than instead of them.
    //
    // It is a LOWER bound on the true supremum, which is attained at a corner
    // built from one point's X and another's Y. Those n^2 corners cost n^3 to
    // test where these n corners cost n^2, and the ranking of one pattern against
    // another survives the approximation.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-discrepancy_sequence
    StarDiscrepancyEstimate(region: Bounds2D, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
        => points.Reduce(0.0, (worst, p) => worst.Max(BoxDiscrepancy(p, region, points)));

    // The periodogram power of one plane wave over the point set: the squared
    // magnitude of the sum of exp(2 pi i f . x), divided by the point count. A
    // Poisson process averages to one at every non-zero frequency, so a reading
    // below one means the pattern SUPPRESSES that frequency and a reading above
    // one means it carries it. Frequencies are in cycles per unit length.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodogram
    WavePower(frequencyX: Number, frequencyY: Number, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
    {
        var cosine = SumOf(points.Map(p => (p.X * frequencyX + p.Y * frequencyY).Turns.Cos));
        var sine = SumOf(points.Map(p => (p.X * frequencyX + p.Y * frequencyY).Turns.Sin));
        return points.Count <= 0 ? 0.0 : (cosine * cosine + sine * sine) / points.Count.ToNumber;
    }

    // The mean power at one frequency magnitude, averaged over `directions`
    // evenly spaced directions across a half turn — power is symmetric, so a
    // whole turn would measure each direction twice. Averaging over direction is
    // what makes the reading a statement about ISOTROPY as well as about
    // frequency content: an axis-aligned pattern that spikes along one direction
    // shows up here as a bump the spacing readings never see.
    RadialPower(frequency: Number, directions: Integer, points: Array<Point2D>): Number
        => directions <= 0 ? 0.0
            : SumOf(directions.MapRange(k =>
                WavePower(frequency * (0.5 * k.ToNumber / directions.ToNumber).Turns.Cos,
                          frequency * (0.5 * k.ToNumber / directions.ToNumber).Turns.Sin,
                          points))) / directions.ToNumber;
```
